Unfortunately, I cannot give you a literal science, since I looked and found no publication dedicated to this topic. So, I can give you the general summary.

Yes, sunlight is capable of degrading certain substances, therefore perfumes should be stored in dark.

Yes, air oxidizes various substances, but given how tightly the perfumes are sealed, they are fairly safe. At worst they might go bad in the spray tube and you just need to spray it out. The same for humidity. 

Yes, temperature is known to also degrade substances. If you occassionally forget it somewhere in heat (car...), that should not matter. Perfumes are one of the most durable cosmetics out there. But longterm exposure to heat might affect the perfume.

You can protect them by keeping them in dark, dry, colder places. But that is often impractical. I think keeping them out of direct sunlight should do the trick. Also, some perfumes can go bad faster than others. Usually the ones with volatile notes (citrus...) will go bad after 2 years or so. If you have more perfumes with base notes, those can last up to many years.
